Geometric mid-domain null for elevational richness

geo_middomain.Rd

Randomises species elevational ranges within a hard domain while keeping each range size fixed (Colwell and Lees 2000), then recomputes richness per elevation band. Compare the observed band richness to the null envelope when testing mid-domain effects on tropical mountains.

Usage

geo_middomain(
  data,
  species = species,
  elevation = elevation,
  bands = 10,
  nperm = 999,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with species occurrences and elevation.

species, elevation

Column selections.

bands

Number of elevation bands, or a numeric vector of breaks.

nperm

Number of null permutations.

seed

Optional RNG seed.

Value

A tibble (tmr_geo_middomain) with band midpoints, observed richness, null mean, and 2.5% / 97.5% null quantiles. Attribute ranges holds the observed species range table.

References

Colwell, R. K. and Lees, D. C. (2000). The mid-domain effect: geometric constraints on the geography of species richness. Trends in Ecology and Evolution, 15, 70-76. doi:10.1016/s0169-5347(99)01767-x

Examples

set.seed(1)
occ <- expand.grid(
  species = paste0("sp", 1:20),
  elevation = seq(200, 3200, by = 200),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
# Each species occupies a contiguous elevational range
occ <- dplyr::filter(
  occ,
  elevation >= 200 + (as.integer(factor(species)) - 1) * 50,
  elevation <= 1200 + (as.integer(factor(species)) - 1) * 80
)
geo_middomain(occ, nperm = 49)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 8
#>     band elevation elev_min elev_max richness null_mean null_lower null_upper
